headline: Local Man Claims To Have Lost His Own Graduation Degree In A 'Particularly Intense' Game Of Paper-Plane Contest
body:
Vikram Varma, a 34-year-old freelance consultant, has sparked a minor social media firestorm after failing to produce his undergraduate degree, which he insists was lost during a high-stakes paper-plane tournament in 2012. Varma’s claim, which has triggered several investigative threads on social media, centres on his inability to provide the document because the original parchment was folded into an ‘aerodynamic fuselage’ for a crucial final-round throw.

“People keep asking for a ‘record’ or a digital certificate from the university, but they don’t understand the structural integrity required to win a professional-tier paper-plane contest,” Varma explained, while holding up a blurry, low-resolution photo of a paper scrap landing in a nearby pond. “That degree wasn't just paper; it was my only chance to defeat my hostel rival, who insisted on using a rigid, non-folded sheet of printer paper.”

When pressed on why he hadn't reached out to the registrar’s office for a duplicate, Varma noted that the process would be ‘too bureaucratic’ and would likely result in an official document that ‘lacked the soul’ of his original, flight-tested certificate. Meanwhile, his college roommate has countered the narrative with a grainy video, claiming the degree was never folded into a plane, but was instead used as a coaster for a celebratory mug of tea that same night.

Critics have pointed out that a degree is typically a standard, verifiable record, but Varma remains steadfast, suggesting that the true value of an education lies not in the ‘bureaucratic validation of a piece of cardstock,’ but in the flight distance one can achieve with it under pressure.
caption: When the degree is lost in the name of aerodynamics. Does your college degree have as much flight time as Vikram's? Tag a classmate who definitely didn't treat their diploma like an origami project. #CollegeLife #DegreeDrama (satire)
igHook: Would you sacrifice your hard-earned degree to win a paper-plane contest?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a crumpled, slightly yellowed piece of heavy paper lying on a wooden study desk next to a spilled cup of tea.

sourceHeadline.title: ‘No record’: Podcaster’s claim reignites row over CJP founder’s BU degree; Dipke hits back with video

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 0 is the only piece that feels like a singular, grounded narrative rather than a repetitive AI attempt to fill the 'man-fails-to-prove-credentials' template. The specific invented detail of folding a degree into an 'aerodynamic fuselage' for a paper-plane contest provides a vivid, absurd, and oddly warm image that avoids the cynical 'podcaster-investigates' tropes used by all other candidates.
